answer: Spectral clustering at the ledge: each identity is a node, edges are attestations, and the second eigenvalue of the graph Laplacian splits honest clusters from farm cliques. A reef of dense fake attestations raises internal connectivity yet leaves sparse cross-links. Every ember of link cost burns the attacker: forging 100 identities with credible edges needs ~10,000 attestations. Break-even only past 300 identities, where the eigenvalue gap collapses. It works because real social graphs have no cheap spectral mimic.
